Cases.Name: The former 45-second wall limit does not stop an advancing LDAP search
5000 raw arrivals over ten minutes remain admissible while progressing
Idle deadline starts at dispatch when no first row has arrived
A stalled search expires after the last raw arrival and retains the diagnostic count
Strict greater-than comparison preserves the former deadline boundary
The hard total cap wins even with a fresh row on every tick
The total cap wins when both idle and total deadlines are exceeded
Configured total duration replaces the default and remains an absolute cap
Missing total duration defaults to 900 seconds
A missing idle duration defaults to 120 seconds for searches
Zero or non-finite deadline settings do not disable bounded operation
Cached queue growth is never treated as raw LDAP progress
Missing or wrong-type progress uses the old elapsed timeout
Malformed, missing and fractional progress fields fail back to a bounded legacy deadline
Future start and future last-row clocks do not reset the deadline
Backwards last-row clocks and inconsistent count/timestamp pairs use bounded fallback
Invalid monotonic now or frequency uses elapsed fallback
The monotonic dispatch clock supersedes wall-clock jumps while valid
A raw arrival during the snapshot cannot be mistaken for a future clock
Actual dispatch timing excludes time previously spent in the scheduler queue
Ordinary jobs retain the former total elapsed deadline and exact message
Writes, queued, cancelled and completed work receive no new expiration effect
The shared progress dictionary is read-only to the decision function
Concurrent session progress dictionaries remain independent
Generic dictionaries and synchronized hashtables follow the same rule
A null job is inert and progress is not inferred from unrelated job members

Limitations: Deterministic pure deadline rules only. No Windows UI, live LDAP, network timing, cancellation or worker integration executed.
